content_sections.body: Prepare a two-turn exchange about speaking about a future activity. Give the main detail, listen to one follow-up, and answer it clearly. Use this model as support: 'I am going to explain the plan slowly and stress the time and place.' The exchange should meet this lesson goal: Use weak forms, thought groups, and key-word stress in a plan.
content_sections.title: Use it in a practical exchange (8 minutes)

content_sections.body: Partner A begins a realistic exchange about speaking about a future activity. Partner B asks for one missing detail. Swap roles and make one change to the time, place, reason, quantity, or next action. Check that the exchange achieves: Use weak forms, thought groups, and key-word stress in a plan.
content_sections.title: Guided dialogue (8 minutes)

content_sections.body: Create a short message about speaking about a future activity without reading the model. Include a main event or plan and one precise detail. Speak it once slowly, then once at a natural pace. Listen for whether the key information is clear.
content_sections.title: Independent response (6 minutes)

exercises.correct_answer: I am going to explain the plan slowly and stress the time and place.
options: I am going to explain the plan slowly and stress the time and place.
Yesterday I left my umbrella on the number 8 bus, then I called the bus office.
What time did the coach leave, and why was it late?
exercises.prompt: Choose the response that gives a clear, useful message for this situation: speaking about a future activity.
Complete the model with the missing words: 'I am going to explain the plan slowly and stress the ____.'
Read this short message for the lesson 'Clear planned speech' and identify the real-life situation it describes.

acceptable_answers: The message is about speaking about a future activity.
questions.question: What situation does the message describe?

exercises.stimulus: I am going to explain the plan slowly and stress the time and place. The message gives one main point and one detail for the listener.

exercises.prompt: Speak for 30–45 seconds about speaking about a future activity. State the main message, add a relevant detail, and answer one follow-up question.

criteria: Communicates the main message about speaking about a future activity clearly.
Adds a relevant detail and responds appropriately to a follow-up question.

language_focus: Use weak forms, thought groups, and key-word stress in a plan.
objectives: Use weak forms, thought groups, and key-word stress in a plan.
Use a main idea and one relevant detail in a response about speaking about a future activity.

listening.answer: The listener should understand that it concerns speaking about a future activity.
constraints: Keep the transcript private before the learner answers the first question.
Use only the supplied transcript; do not require media.
listening.goal: Identify the situation and a useful detail in a short message about speaking about a future activity.
listening.instruction: Listen once to a short message about speaking about a future activity. Answer the question before the transcript is revealed, then listen again and check the key detail.
listening.question: What is the message mainly about?
listening.transcript: I am going to explain the plan slowly and stress the time and place.

constraints: Assess pronunciation only when learner audio is supplied.
Return NOT_ASSESSED when learner audio is unavailable.
pronunciation.goal: Make the key information in speaking about a future activity easy to hear.
pronunciation.instruction: Say the model for speaking about a future activity in two thought groups. Mark the pause between ideas, then stress the word that gives the key action, time, quantity, reason, or request. Record a second attempt after listening to your first attempt.
pronunciation.target: Thought-group pause and key-word stress in clear planned speech

constraints: Name the learner and tutor roles before the first turn.
Use at most three tutor turns and stop after the agreed next step.
speaking.goal: Complete a clear, practical exchange about speaking about a future activity.
speaking.instruction: Roleplay speaking about a future activity. Learner role: explain the situation and give one useful detail. Tutor role: be a helpful listener, ask one specific follow-up, and confirm the next step. Begin with a natural greeting and finish once both roles agree on the next action.

constraints: Wait for the learner draft before giving feedback.
Give concise feedback only; do not replace the learner draft.
writing.goal: Write a connected, useful short message about speaking about a future activity.
writing.instruction: Write a 35–50 word message about speaking about a future activity. Include the main event or plan, one precise detail, and the next action or response. Submit your own draft before requesting feedback.

title: Clear planned speech
